what_happened: The person running Athena deleted by hand the 19 GB build folder left by the first, interrupted run of the merge-refusal job (20261102-001719-1fva). The the person running Athena had cut that run off. Free disk had fallen to 1.4 GB while the retry was building. No acceptance criterion or check had failed. It was an environment stop. The sweep that removes builds of interrupted jobs runs only at drain start, and this retry ran outside a drain.
cause: Athena still has no disk lifecycle that holds for every way a job runs. Cleanup of regenerable build folders is tied to one event (drain start) instead of to the build's own state. An interrupted job's build is orphaned as soon as the job is cut off, but nothing reclaims it when a retry starts, when a build begins, or while free space falls. A retry outside a drain therefore stacks a second large build on the first one and meets the disk limit. The free-space guard only reports a low-disk stop and frees nothing. This is the sixth hand cleanup in this class in a few days.
prevention: Make Athena own the build-folder lifecycle in one place that every run path calls, not only drain start. Before any retry or new build starts, and before the checks stage, Athena removes the build folders of jobs that are interrupted, abandoned, finished or superseded. A job's retry deletes its own previous attempt's build before building. Athena also counts remaining build size against a disk budget and runs the same reclaim when free space falls under a threshold. It must never remove the build of a job that is running now. The reclaim and each deletion are logged, so no the person running Athena cleanup is needed.
proposed_request: Make Athena reclaim regenerable build folders automatically on every run path, not only at drain start. Outcome: no the person running Athena needs to delete build folders by hand to keep a job from running out of disk. Done when: (1) starting a retry of a job removes that job's earlier attempts' build folders before the new build begins, whether or not a drain is running; (2) the interrupted-job sweep runs at the start of any command that builds (retry, run, drain), not only at drain start; (3) the sweep removes builds of interrupted, abandoned, finished and superseded jobs and never touches the build of a job that is currently running, shown by a test with one running job and one interrupted job; (4) the sweep runs again before the checks stage when free disk is under the configured guard, and logs each folder removed and the bytes freed; (5) a test starts a retry outside a drain with a leftover interrupted build and shows the leftover is gone before the new build starts. Keep the change within the disk and cleanup code and its tests, and add a changelog entry.
